title: Lock-in as a decision, not an accident

videos.script: People say lock-in the way they say debt. As if it were always a mistake. {{kinds}} This lesson takes it apart. There are four kinds. What your code says, where your data is, what your team knows, and what you signed. Each one is bought with something you wanted, and each compute choice in this course carries a different mix. {{seam}} Then you build a seam. One small rule for the shop, and two thin adapters around it. You run it as a web server, and as a Lambda function in AWS's own runtime, on your laptop. Same answer, to the cent. {{cost}} Next, an estimate of what leaving would cost. Lines of code to rewrite, gigabytes to move at the price AWS publishes, and people who would have to learn a new platform. The biggest line is rarely the one people expect. {{record}} And last, a decision record. The lock-in the shop accepts, what it refuses, and the numbers that would make it change its mind.
